chunks: As for that which indicates the invalidity of the statement of the Kaisaniyya, who believe in the Imamate of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, there are many things.

key_terms.إِمَامَة: Imamate, the divine leadership and authority of the Imams
key_terms.الكَيسَانِيَّة: Kaisaniyya, a Shia sect believing Imamate passed to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah
key_terms.فَسَاد: Invalidity or flaw in a theological statement
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, son of Imam Ali and Hanifa

ai.seo_question: What are the arguments against the Kaisaniyya belief in the Imamate of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi begins his systematic dismantling of the Kaisaniyya sect by presenting the primary evidences that invalidate their claim that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah was the designated Imam. This introduction sets the stage for a rigorous theological refutation, distinguishing the Shia view of explicit designation (Nass) from the Kaisaniyya's specific interpretation of the Prophet's brother's son as the Mahdi.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Arguments proving the invalidity of Kaisaniyya, who believe in the Imamate of Muhammad Ibne Hanafiyyah, are many.
